title: Leaks Hard To Find, Experts Say
author: Harry Berkowitz
summary: Article discusses the difficulty of investigating government leaks and the ethics involved in publishing leaked information, specifically in the context of a leak revealing a CIA operative's identity. Jay Rosen is quoted as an expert on journalism ethics.
excerpt: "The problem in cases like this is that there may be certain news value in what the leaker is offering, but there may be more news value in the fact that the person is trying to leak it," said Professor Jay Rosen of the New York University journalism department.
pull_quote: The problem in cases like this is that there may be certain news value in what the leaker is offering, but there may be more news value in the fact that the person is trying to leak it.

title: 'Choice' pays too little attention to issues
author: Peter S. Canellos
thematic_categories: Press & Media Criticism, Journalism Theory & Practice
summary: A review of Bob Woodward's book 'The Choice' discusses the book's focus on campaign strategy rather than issues. Jay Rosen is quoted as a public journalism leader criticizing the book's premise and focus on political consultants.
excerpt: "I find it interesting that he assumes the mystery of politics that needs investigating is how these professional consultants work," Rosen said. "Of all the things Americans need to investigate about their politics these days, that doesn't seem high on the list."
pull_quote: I find it interesting that he assumes the mystery of politics that needs investigating is how these professional consultants work. Of all the things Americans need to investigate about their politics these days, that doesn't seem high on the list.
